summary: Dewey Helper for LibraryThing: a free browser tool for small libraries that reads your own catalogue export, extracts ISBNs locally and looks up Dewey numbers in batches from Open Library — the 2026 successor to an OCLC Classify workflow discontinued in 2024, with no scraping or automated logins.

props.title: How it works
steps: Export your LibraryThing catalogue as XLSX, TSV, CSV or JSON.
Open Dewey Helper and choose the file.
ISBNs are extracted locally in your browser.
Press Find Dewey numbers to send batched ISBN lookups to Open Library.

props.title: Dewey Helper
props.text: The exact ISBN edition is checked first before falling back to related editions.

props.title: Why rebuild it?
props.q: Why did the original converter workflow stop working?
props.explain: OCLC Classify shut down in 2024, so the new tool uses Open Library and avoids automating LibraryThing edits.

summary: famhist: a private family-history research system for working with an AI agent — every person attached by a record, every conclusion backed by a citation or a bounded negative, GEDCOM edit queues and evidence reports checked by scripts, a handbook of standards, and strict handling of living people.

props.on: Every person shown is attached by a record — no record, no branch.

props.title: Rule of evidence
props.q: What must stand behind every conclusion in the tree?
options: A citation or a bounded negative
props.explain: Conclusions need a citation, or a bounded negative search showing what was checked and not found.

props.text: Changes to the tree are queued as scripted edits and checked by tools, not remembered by hand.

summary: A local-first archive for ChatGPT data exports: it imports the official ZIP, keeps the full conversation node graph — regenerations, edited and abandoned branches — reconstructs the current transcript, and stores everything in SQLite with FTS5 search, never uploading anything.

props.title: Import
steps: Drop in the official ChatGPT export ZIP.
Every node keeps its parent-child pointer.
Regenerations and edited branches are preserved.
The current transcript follows the true current_node lineage.

props.text: Alternative branches are kept, not flattened — you can walk back to a regenerated reply.

props.title: Privacy
props.q: Where does your conversation history go?
options: Nowhere — it stays in a local SQLite file
props.explain: Everything is stored and searched locally.

summary: pdfresearch: local-first processing for huge merged research PDFs — page-level deduplication with a provenance map, document-boundary detection from running headers and page-number resets, splitting, privacy flagging, and an evaluation harness. Code only; personal documents never enter the repo.

props.title: Duplicates
props.q: What happens to a duplicate page?
options: It is recorded in the provenance map against its canonical page
props.explain: Every original page maps to a canonical page, so nothing is silently lost.

props.text: Pages that look like health, NDIS or banking material are flagged; the repository is code-only.

props.title: Pipeline
steps: Map provenance and evaluate against fixtures.

props.title: Food-safety log (5–60 °C)
steps: Start a guided cook: the log records time the batch spends between 5 and 60 °C.

Same-batch entries persist so leftovers keep their history.
Status turns amber at 2 hours and red at 4 hours — storage completion is blocked until it is safe.
